html:
The Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan began in 1820, when Muhammad Ali, the ruler of Egypt, sent an army under his son Ismail up the Nile, ending the Funj sultanate of Sennar in 1821.

Muhammad Ali wanted gold and slaves for his new army. The Egyptians founded Khartoum as their capital, taxed the farmers of the north heavily, and pushed south and west, taking Darfur in 1874.

Traders and soldiers raided the south for ivory and slaves, and under Khedive Ismail European officers such as Charles Gordon were hired to govern and to fight the slave trade. Anger at taxes, foreign officials and the attack on the slave trade fed the rising of the Mahdi in 1881, which ended Egyptian rule over Sudan.
sum: The Turco-Egyptian conquest of Sudan began in 1820, when Muhammad Ali, the ruler of Egypt, sent an army under his son Ismail up the Nile, ending the Funj sultanate of Sennar in 1821.
